what: OT/BG (2026-10-21): the first run of the sixteen backend-optimality experiments PR #821 proposes (docs/research/BCIR_BACKEND_OPTIMALITY_AND_KERNEL_GATES_2026-10-20.md on its branch, at c01a53c8), under the measurement contract tools/perf/ot_contract.py holds (BG0): every experiment's record -- measured where this host and the repository hold what it needs, unavailable naming the capabilities the host lacks, blocked naming the prerequisite the repository lacks -- and the eight gates stated over them and the GEM+ rows they read. The records are tools/perf/ot_run.py's; the gates read gemplus_baseline.py's train rows (rows.json).
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 vCPUs; capabilities cpu, numpy; Python 3.11.15, NumPy 2.2.6, Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1). The run names the commit it ran on (764e7f3578ea662ce4c53ba4fb9575dc767ec33d). The interpreter that ran has neither PyTorch nor Triton, and the host has no GPU, QEMU, multi-device host, physical device rig or readable PMU: those experiments are unavailable, never simulated. Under an interpreter that has PyTorch and Triton (checked here with the model-lab pin, torch 2.13.0, and Triton 3.7.1) the same run records OT-02, OT-05, OT-10 and OT-11 blocked -- their runners are not in this tree yet -- and never fails. Wall times are indicative: one virtualized host, one process at a time.

records.ot.json: tools/perf/ot_run.py's output: the sixteen records, the host's capabilities, the rows the gates read and each gate's state with what it lacks
records.rows.json: tools/perf/gemplus_baseline.py --compare --group train --json: the GEM+ rows BG1 reads
